column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|09-28|1841|Ζωρζ Κλεμανσώ|Georges Clemenceau|Georges Clemenceau was a French politician. As prime minister at the end of the First World War he led France to victory and was called "the Tiger". He took part in the Treaty of Versailles. He died in 1929.
bio|09-28|1891|Χέρμαν Μέλβιλ|Herman Melville|Herman Melville was an American writer. He died in 1891 in New York. "Moby-Dick" was recognised as a masterpiece after his death.

bio|09-28|1895|Λουί Παστέρ|Louis Pasteur|Louis Pasteur was a French chemist and microbiologist. He developed vaccines against rabies and anthrax, proved the role of microorganisms in disease and introduced pasteurisation. He died in 1895.
bio|09-28|1924|Μαρτσέλλο Μαστρογιάννι|Marcello Mastroianni|Marcello Mastroianni was an Italian actor. He became known with Fellini's films "La Dolce Vita" and "8½". He died in 1996.

bio|09-28|1934|Μπριζίτ Μπαρντό|Brigitte Bardot|Brigitte Bardot is a French actress and singer, a symbol of French cinema in the 1950s and 1960s. She became known with the film "And God Created Woman". Later she devoted herself to the protection of animals.

bio|09-28|1947|Σεΐχ Χασίνα|Sheikh Hasina|Sheikh Hasina is a Bangladeshi politician and the daughter of the country's founder, Mujibur Rahman. She was prime minister of Bangladesh for many years, until 2024, when she was forced to leave the country after popular protests.

bio|09-28|1970|Γκαμάλ Άμπντελ Νάσερ|Gamal Abdel Nasser|Gamal Abdel Nasser was an Egyptian politician. He was president of Egypt from 1956 to 1970, nationalised the Suez Canal and led the pan-Arab movement. He died in 1970.
bio|09-28|1989|Φερδινάντο Μάρκος|Ferdinand Marcos|Ferdinand Marcos died in 1989 in Honolulu, in exile. He was president of the Philippines from 1965 to 1986 and ruled as a dictator.

bio|09-29|1547|Μιγκέλ ντε Θερβάντες|Miguel de Cervantes|Miguel de Cervantes was a Spanish writer. He wrote "Don Quixote", which is regarded as the first modern novel. His birth date, 29 September, is probable but not certain. He died in 1616.

bio|09-29|1901|Ενρίκο Φέρμι|Enrico Fermi|Enrico Fermi was an Italian physicist. He built the first nuclear reactor in 1942 and in 1938 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He contributed to the Manhattan Project. He died in 1954.

bio|09-29|1902|Εμίλ Ζολά|Émile Zola|Émile Zola was a French writer of naturalism. He wrote the cycle "Rougon-Macquart" and the text "J'accuse" about the Dreyfus affair. He died in 1902, from carbon monoxide poisoning.

bio|09-29|1913|Ρούντολφ Ντίζελ|Rudolf Diesel|Rudolf Diesel was a German engineer. He invented the diesel engine and disappeared in 1913 while travelling by ship across the English Channel. The circumstances of his death were never clarified.

bio|09-29|1936|Σίλβιο Μπερλουσκόνι|Silvio Berlusconi|Silvio Berlusconi was an Italian businessman and politician. He was prime minister of Italy three times and owner of Milan and of the Mediaset television networks. He died in 2023.

bio|09-29|1943|Λεχ Βαλέσα|Lech Wałęsa|Lech Wałęsa is a Polish electrician and politician. He led the "Solidarity" trade union and was president of Poland from 1990 to 1995. In 1983 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|09-29|1951|Μιτσέλ Μπατσελέ|Michelle Bachelet|Michelle Bachelet is a Chilean doctor and politician. She was the first woman president of Chile, from 2006 to 2010 and again from 2014 to 2018. She also served as United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights.
bio|09-29|1973|Ουίσταν Ώντεν|W. H. Auden|Wystan Hugh Auden was a British-American poet. He wrote "The Age of Anxiety" and the poem "Funeral Blues". He died in 1973.
bio|09-29|2012|Ήβη Καμάργο|Hebe Camargo|Hebe Camargo was a Brazilian singer and television presenter, one of the best-known personalities of Brazilian television. She died in 2012.

bio|09-30|420|Ιερώνυμος|Jerome|Jerome was a Christian theologian and translator. He translated the Bible into Latin, in the version known as the Vulgate, and he spent his last years in Bethlehem. He died in 420.

bio|09-30|1207|Ρουμί|Rumi|Jalal al-Din Rumi was a Persian poet and mystic. He wrote the "Masnavi" and founded the order of the whirling dervishes, based in Konya. He died in 1273. His date of birth is the traditional one.

bio|09-30|1897|Τερέζ ντε Λισιέ|Thérèse of Lisieux|Thérèse of Lisieux was a French Carmelite nun. She died young, at the age of 24, and her autobiography, "Story of a Soul", became very well known. The Catholic Church declared her a saint in 1925.
bio|09-30|1924|Τρούμαν Καπότε|Truman Capote|Truman Capote was an American writer. He wrote "Breakfast at Tiffany's" and "In Cold Blood". He died in 1984.

bio|09-30|1928|Έλι Βίζελ|Elie Wiesel|Elie Wiesel was born in Romania and was a survivor of Auschwitz and Buchenwald. He wrote the book "Night", and in 1986 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 2016.

bio|09-30|1955|Τζέιμς Ντιν|James Dean|James Dean was an American actor. He became a symbol of youth with the films "East of Eden" and "Rebel Without a Cause". He was killed in a car accident in 1955, at the age of 24.
bio|09-30|1964|Μόνικα Μπελλούτσι|Monica Bellucci|Monica Bellucci is an Italian actress and model. She has appeared in films such as "Malèna", "The Matrix Reloaded" and "The Passion of the Christ".

bio|09-30|1990|Πάτρικ Γουάιτ|Patrick White|Patrick White was an Australian writer. He wrote the novels "The Death of the Traveller" and "The Gaze of the Blind". In 1973 he became the first Australian to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1990.

bio|09-30|1997|Μαξ Φερστάπεν|Max Verstappen|Max Verstappen is a Dutch racing driver. He won the Formula One World Championship with Red Bull for the first time in 2021, and again in the following years.

bio|10-01|1499|Μαρσίλιο Φιτσίνο|Marsilio Ficino|Marsilio Ficino was an Italian philosopher of the Renaissance. He translated the works of Plato into Latin and led the Platonic Academy of Florence with the support of the Medici. He died in 1499.

bio|10-01|1684|Πιερ Κορνέιγ|Pierre Corneille|Pierre Corneille was a French playwright. He wrote the tragicomedy "The Cid" and other tragedies. Together with Racine he is regarded as one of the great figures of French classical tragedy. He died in 1684.

bio|10-01|1924|Τζίμι Κάρτερ|Jimmy Carter|Jimmy Carter was the 39th president of the United States, from 1977 to 1981. He mediated the Camp David Accords and in 2002 was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 2024, at the age of 100.
bio|10-01|1935|Τζούλι Άντριους|Julie Andrews|Julie Andrews is an English actress and singer. She won an Oscar for "Mary Poppins" and starred in "The Sound of Music".

bio|10-01|1956|Τερέζα Μέι|Theresa May|Theresa May is a British Conservative politician. She was prime minister of the United Kingdom from 2016 to 2019 and led the country through the negotiations on Brexit.

bio|10-01|1966|Τζορτζ Γουεά|George Weah|George Weah is a former Liberian footballer and politician. He played for Milan and Paris Saint-Germain, and in 1995 he won the Ballon d'Or. He became president of Liberia in 2018.

bio|10-01|2012|Έρικ Χομπσμπάουμ|Eric Hobsbawm|Eric Hobsbawm was a British historian. He wrote the four-volume series on the "long nineteenth century" and "The Age of Extremes" on the short twentieth century. He died in 2012.
bio|10-01|2013|Τομ Κλάνσυ|Tom Clancy|Tom Clancy was an American writer. He wrote novels with military and espionage themes, such as "The Hunt for Red October". He died in 2013.

bio|10-02|1847|Πάουλ φον Χίντενμπουργκ|Paul von Hindenburg|Paul von Hindenburg was born in 1847. He was a German field marshal in the First World War and President of Germany from 1925. He appointed Hitler chancellor in 1933. He died in 1934.
bio|10-02|1853|Φρανσουά Αραγκό|François Arago|François Arago was a French mathematician, physicist and astronomer. He studied light and magnetism and was also a politician. He died in 1853.

bio|10-02|1869|Μαχάτμα Γκάντι|Mahatma Gandhi|Mohandas Gandhi, known as Mahatma, was the leader of the movement for India's independence from Britain. He used peaceful, non-violent resistance. He was assassinated in 1948.

bio|10-02|1890|Γκράουτσο Μαρξ|Groucho Marx|Groucho Marx was an American comedian and actor, one of the Marx Brothers. He became known for his witty humour and his moustache, in films such as "Duck Soup". He died in 1977.
bio|10-02|1904|Γκράχαμ Γκρην|Graham Greene|Graham Greene was an English writer. He wrote the novels "The Third Man", "The Power and the Glory" and "The Quiet American". He died in 1991.

bio|10-02|1927|Σβάντε Αρρένιους|Svante Arrhenius|Svante Arrhenius was a Swedish chemist. He formulated the theory of electrolytic dissociation and studied the greenhouse effect. In 1903 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1927.

bio|10-02|1951|Στινγκ|Sting|Sting, whose real name is Gordon Sumner, is an English singer, bassist and actor. He was the leader of The Police and continues as a solo artist, with hits such as "Every Breath You Take".

bio|10-02|1968|Μαρσέλ Ντυσάν|Marcel Duchamp|Marcel Duchamp was a French painter and sculptor and a pioneer of Dada. He became known for his "readymades", such as "Fountain", a urinal, and he overturned the concept of the work of art. He died in 1968.
bio|10-02|1973|Πάαβο Νούρμι|Paavo Nurmi|Paavo Nurmi was a Finnish long-distance runner. He won nine Olympic gold medals in the 1920s and became known as "the Flying Finn". He died in 1973.

bio|10-03|1226|Φραγκίσκος της Ασίζης|Francis of Assisi|Francis of Assisi was an Italian monk and the founder of the Franciscan order. He lived in poverty, loved nature and preached peace. He died in 1226 and was canonised two years later.

bio|10-03|1895|Σεργκέι Γεσένιν|Sergei Yesenin|Sergei Yesenin was a Russian poet with a lyrical and rural inspiration. He was briefly married to Isadora Duncan. He took his own life in 1925, at the age of 30.

bio|10-03|1897|Λουί Αραγκόν|Louis Aragon|Louis Aragon was a French poet and writer. He was a founding member of surrealism and later a member of the Communist Party. He wrote "Le Paysan de Paris". He died in 1982.
bio|10-03|1900|Τόμας Γουλφ|Thomas Wolfe|Thomas Wolfe was an American writer. He wrote the novels "Look Homeward, Angel" and "Of Time and the River". He died young, at the age of 37, in 1938.

bio|10-03|1929|Γκούσταβ Στρέζεμαν|Gustav Stresemann|Gustav Stresemann was a German politician. As chancellor and foreign minister of the Weimar Republic he promoted reconciliation with France. In 1926 he shared the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1929.
bio|10-03|1969|Γκουέν Στεφάνι|Gwen Stefani|Gwen Stefani is an American singer. She was the lead singer of the band No Doubt and continued as a solo artist, with hits such as "Hollaback Girl".

bio|10-03|1981|Ζλάταν Ιμπραΐμοβιτς|Zlatan Ibrahimović|Zlatan Ibrahimović is a former Swedish footballer who played as a forward. He played for Ajax, Inter, Barcelona, Paris Saint-Germain and Milan, and he scored more than 500 goals.
bio|10-03|1987|Ζαν Ανούιγ|Jean Anouilh|Jean Anouilh was a French playwright. He wrote "Antigone" in 1944, an adaptation of the ancient myth. He died in 1987.
bio|10-03|2017|Τζαλάλ Ταλαμπανί|Jalal Talabani|Jalal Talabani was a Kurdish politician from Iraq. He led the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan and was president of Iraq from 2005 to 2014. He died in 2017.
bio|10-04|1669|Ρέμπραντ|Rembrandt|Rembrandt van Rijn died in 1669 in Amsterdam. He was a Dutch painter of the Golden Age, known for his portraits and for his technique of light and shadow.

bio|10-04|1822|Ράδερφορντ Χέιζ|Rutherford B. Hayes|Rutherford B. Hayes was the 19th president of the United States, from 1877 to 1881. He was elected after a disputed election and put an end to Reconstruction. He died in 1893.

bio|10-04|1895|Μπάστερ Κίτον|Buster Keaton|Buster Keaton was an American actor and director of silent cinema. He became known as "the man who never smiled" and performed dangerous stunts himself, in films such as "The General". He died in 1966.

bio|10-04|1903|Όττο Βάινινγκερ|Otto Weininger|Otto Weininger was an Austrian philosopher. He wrote the book "Sex and Character", with particularly controversial views, and he took his own life in 1903, at the age of 23.

bio|10-04|1916|Βιτάλι Γκίνζμπουργκ|Vitaly Ginzburg|Vitaly Ginzburg was a Russian physicist. He contributed to the theory of superconductivity and in 2003 shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 2009.
bio|10-04|1923|Τσάρλτον Ίστον|Charlton Heston|Charlton Heston was an American actor. He played Moses in "The Ten Commandments" and won an Oscar for "Ben-Hur". He died in 2008.
bio|10-04|1946|Σούζαν Σαράντον|Susan Sarandon|Susan Sarandon is an American actress. She appeared in films including "Thelma & Louise", and she won an Oscar for "Dead Man Walking".

bio|10-04|1947|Μαξ Πλανκ|Max Planck|Max Planck was a German physicist and the founder of quantum theory. In 1900 he introduced the concept of energy quanta, and in 1918 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1947.

bio|10-04|1970|Τζάνις Τζόπλιν|Janis Joplin|Janis Joplin was an American rock and blues singer with a powerful voice. She became known with "Piece of My Heart". She died in 1970, at the age of 27, from an overdose.
bio|10-05|1285|Φίλιππος Γ'|Philip III|Philip III, "the Bold", was King of France from 1270. He took part in the Eighth Crusade and the Aragonese Crusade. He died in 1285 on the return journey.

bio|10-05|1713|Ντενί Ντιντερό|Denis Diderot|Denis Diderot was a French philosopher of the Enlightenment and the publisher of the "Encyclopédie". He wrote "Rameau's Nephew" and "Jacques the Fatalist". He died in 1784.

bio|10-05|1829|Τσέστερ Άρθουρ|Chester A. Arthur|Chester A. Arthur was the 21st president of the United States. He took office in 1881 after the assassination of Garfield and promoted reform of the public sector. He died in 1886.

bio|10-05|1880|Ζακ Όφενμπαχ|Jacques Offenbach|Jacques Offenbach was a German-French composer. He wrote operettas, such as "Orpheus in the Underworld", and the opera "The Tales of Hoffmann". He died in 1880.

bio|10-05|1936|Βάτσλαβ Χάβελ|Václav Havel|Václav Havel was a Czech writer and politician. He was a dissident in Communist Czechoslovakia and became president after the Velvet Revolution of 1989. He died in 2011.
bio|10-05|1952|Ιμομάλι Ραχμόν|Emomali Rahmon|Emomali Rahmon has been president of Tajikistan since 1992. He is one of the longest-serving leaders in Central Asia.
bio|10-05|1975|Κέιτ Γουίνσλετ|Kate Winslet|Kate Winslet is an English actress. She became known with "Titanic" and won an Oscar for "The Reader".
bio|10-05|2011|Στηβ Τζομπς|Steve Jobs|Steve Jobs was an American entrepreneur and co-founder of Apple. He led the development of the iPod, the iPhone and the iPad. He died in 2011 of cancer.
bio|10-06|877|Κάρολος ο Φαλακρός|Charles the Bald|Charles the Bald was King of West Francia from 843, and Emperor from 875. He was the grandson of Charlemagne. He died in 877.

bio|10-06|1773|Λουδοβίκος Φίλιππος|Louis Philippe|Louis Philippe was King of the French from 1830 to 1848. He was known as the "Citizen King" and was overthrown by the February Revolution. He died in 1850.

bio|10-06|1846|Τζορτζ Ουέστινγκχαουζ|George Westinghouse|George Westinghouse was an American inventor and businessman. He invented the air brake for trains and promoted alternating current in his dispute with Edison. He died in 1914.
bio|10-06|1887|Λε Κορμπυζιέ|Le Corbusier|Le Corbusier was born in Switzerland as Charles-Édouard Jeanneret. He was an architect and theorist, a pioneer of modernism. He died in 1965.
bio|10-06|1892|Άλφρεντ Τέννυσον|Alfred Tennyson|Alfred Tennyson died in 1892. He was an English poet and court poet for almost 42 years, and he wrote "Idylls of the King".

bio|10-06|1903|Έρνεστ Τόμας Σάιντον Γουόλτον|Ernest Walton|Ernest Walton was an Irish physicist. Together with John Cockcroft he was the first to split the atomic nucleus by artificial acceleration of particles, and in 1951 they were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1995.

bio|10-06|1914|Θορ Χέιερνταλ|Thor Heyerdahl|Thor Heyerdahl was a Norwegian explorer. With the raft "Kon-Tiki" he crossed the Pacific in 1947, to show that migration from South America had been possible. He died in 2002.

bio|10-06|1981|Ανουάρ Σαντάτ|Anwar Sadat|Anwar Sadat was president of Egypt from 1970. He launched the Yom Kippur War in 1973 and in 1979 signed a peace treaty with Israel. He shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Begin. He was assassinated on 6 October 1981.

bio|10-06|1989|Μπέτι Ντέιβις|Bette Davis|Bette Davis was an American actress. She won two Oscars, for "Dangerous" and "Jezebel", and she starred in "What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?". She died in 1989.
bio|10-07|929|Κάρολος Γ΄ ο Απλός|Charles the Simple|Charles the Simple was King of the West Franks from 898. He gave Normandy to the Viking Rollo. He was deposed in 923 and died in captivity in 929.

bio|10-07|1849|Έντγκαρ Άλλαν Πόε|Edgar Allan Poe|Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer and poet. He wrote the poem "The Raven" and stories such as "The Black Cat", and he is regarded as a pioneer of detective fiction. He died in 1849 in Baltimore.

bio|10-07|1885|Νιλς Μπορ|Niels Bohr|Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist. He developed the Bohr model of the atom and contributed to quantum mechanics. In 1922 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1962.

bio|10-07|1900|Χάινριχ Χίμλερ|Heinrich Himmler|Heinrich Himmler was a German Nazi official. As head of the SS and the Gestapo he was responsible for the concentration camps and the Holocaust. He took his own life in 1945, when he was arrested.
bio|10-07|1931|Ντέσμοντ Τούτου|Desmond Tutu|Desmond Tutu was a South African archbishop of Cape Town and an activist against apartheid. In 1984 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 2021.

bio|10-07|1952|Βλαντίμιρ Πούτιν|Vladimir Putin|Vladimir Putin was born in Leningrad and is a Russian politician. A former KGB officer, he has been president of Russia since 2012, and since 2000 he has held the posts of prime minister and president.
bio|10-07|1988|Ντιέγκο Κόστα|Diego Costa|Diego Costa is a footballer born in Brazil who played for the Spain national team. He played as a forward for Atlético Madrid and Chelsea.

bio|10-07|2006|Άννα Πολιτκόφσκαγια|Anna Politkovskaya|Anna Politkovskaya was a Russian journalist. She wrote about the war in Chechnya and about violations of human rights. She was murdered in 2006 in Moscow.
bio|10-07|2011|Ραμίζ Αλία|Ramiz Alia|Ramiz Alia was an Albanian politician. He succeeded Enver Hoxha in 1985 and led Albania until the fall of communism in 1992. He died in 2011.
bio|10-08|1754|Χένρυ Φήλντινγκ|Henry Fielding|Henry Fielding was an English writer. He wrote "Tom Jones" and was also a judge. He died in 1754 in Lisbon.

bio|10-08|1869|Φράνκλιν Πιρς|Franklin Pierce|Franklin Pierce was the 14th president of the United States, from 1853 to 1857. His term was marked by the dispute over slavery, which led to the Civil War. He died in 1869.

bio|10-08|1895|Χουάν Περόν|Juan Perón|Juan Perón was an Argentine general and politician. He was president of Argentina, was overthrown in 1955 and returned in 1973. He died in 1974. Peronism continues to influence Argentine politics.
bio|10-08|1949|Σιγκούρνι Γουίβερ|Sigourney Weaver|Sigourney Weaver is an American actress. She became known as Ripley in the film "Alien" and its sequels, and she also appeared in "Avatar".

bio|10-08|1958|Ούρσουλα φον ντερ Λάιεν|Ursula von der Leyen|Ursula von der Leyen is a German politician and physician. She was Germany's minister of defence and since 2019 has been president of the European Commission, the first woman to hold the post.
bio|10-08|1967|Κλέμεντ Άττλη|Clement Attlee|Clement Attlee was a British Labour politician. He was prime minister from 1945 to 1951 and founded the National Health Service. He died in 1967.

bio|10-08|1970|Ματ Ντέιμον|Matt Damon|Matt Damon is an American actor and screenwriter. He won the Oscar for Best Original Screenplay for "Good Will Hunting" and starred in the "Bourne" series and in "Interstellar".
bio|10-08|1985|Bruno Mars|Bruno Mars|Bruno Mars is an American singer and songwriter. He became known with hits such as "Just the Way You Are" and "Uptown Funk", and he has won many Grammy awards.

bio|10-08|1992|Βίλι Μπραντ|Willy Brandt|Willy Brandt was a German Social Democratic politician. He was chancellor of West Germany from 1969 to 1974 and began the "Ostpolitik". In 1971 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 1992.
bio|10-09|1879|Μαξ φον Λάουε|Max von Laue|Max von Laue was a German physicist. He discovered the diffraction of X-rays by crystals and in 1914 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1960.

bio|10-09|1892|Ίβο Άντριτς|Ivo Andrić|Ivo Andrić was a Yugoslav writer from Bosnia. He wrote the novel "The Bridge on the Drina" and in 1961 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1975.

bio|10-09|1906|Λεοπόλντ Σεντάρ Σανγκόρ|Léopold Sédar Senghor|Léopold Sédar Senghor was a Senegalese poet and politician. He was the first president of Senegal after independence in 1960 and a theorist of "négritude". He died in 2001.

bio|10-09|1940|Τζον Λένον|John Lennon|John Lennon was born in 1940 in Liverpool. He was a co-founder of the Beatles and had a solo career with songs such as "Imagine". He was murdered in New York in 1980.

bio|10-09|1943|Πιέτερ Ζέεμαν|Pieter Zeeman|Pieter Zeeman was a Dutch physicist. He discovered the Zeeman effect, the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field, and in 1902 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Lorentz. He died in 1943.

bio|10-09|1966|Ντέιβιντ Κάμερον|David Cameron|David Cameron is a British Conservative politician. He was prime minister of the United Kingdom from 2010 to 2016 and resigned after the Brexit referendum.

bio|10-09|1967|Ερνέστο Τσε Γκεβάρα|Ernesto "Che" Guevara|Ernesto "Che" Guevara was born in Argentina and was a doctor and revolutionary. He took part in the Cuban Revolution. He was captured in Bolivia and executed on 9 October 1967.

bio|10-09|1974|Όσκαρ Σίντλερ|Oskar Schindler|Oskar Schindler was a German businessman. During the Second World War he saved more than 1,000 Jewish workers of his factory from the extermination camps. He died in 1974.
bio|10-09|1978|Ζακ Μπρελ|Jacques Brel|Jacques Brel was a Belgian singer-songwriter. He wrote and sang hits such as "Ne me quitte pas", and he also acted in films. He died in 1978.

bio|10-10|680|Χουσεΐν ιμπν Αλί|Husayn ibn Ali|Husayn ibn Ali was the grandson of the prophet Muhammad and a leading figure for the Shia. He was killed in 680 at the Battle of Karbala. The day of his death is commemorated every year by the Shia as Ashura.
bio|10-10|1470|Σελίμ Α΄|Selim I|Selim I was an Ottoman sultan from 1512 to 1520. He conquered Syria and Egypt and took the title of caliph. He was the father of Suleiman the Magnificent.
bio|10-10|1659|Άμπελ Τάσμαν|Abel Tasman|Abel Tasman was a Dutch navigator. In 1642 he was the first European to reach Tasmania and New Zealand. He died in 1659.

bio|10-10|1731|Χένρι Κάβεντις|Henry Cavendish|Henry Cavendish was a British scientist. He discovered hydrogen and measured the gravitational constant with the Cavendish experiment. He was extremely solitary. He died in 1810.
bio|10-10|1813|Τζουζέπε Βέρντι|Giuseppe Verdi|Giuseppe Verdi was an Italian composer. He wrote operas such as "Rigoletto", "La Traviata", "Il Trovatore" and "Aida". He died in 1901.
